title: Philippines Central Bank Proposes 12-Month Freeze on Payment Operator Registrations
dek: The Philippine central bank has proposed a 12-month freeze on new payment operator registrations and stricter controls on arrangements involving virtual asset service providers. The move signals tighter gatekeeping and surveillance of crypto-adjacent payment flows during a period of global VASP regulatory crackdowns.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: The central bank proposes a 12-month freeze on new payment operator registrations and enhanced monitoring plus transaction limits for arrangements involving VASPs.
bottom_line: The Philippine freeze creates a near-term bottleneck for VASP access to domestic payment rails. Track whether the moratorium extends beyond 12 months or becomes permanent, and whether other major emerging-market regulators adopt similar holding patterns.
body: The Philippine central bank has proposed a 12-month freeze on new payment operator registrations, according to Cointelegraph's reporting on September 7, 2026. The proposal includes enhanced monitoring and transaction limits for arrangements involving virtual asset service providers, the outlet reports.

The move signals stricter gatekeeping of crypto-adjacent payment flows at a time when regulators across multiple jurisdictions are tightening oversight of VASP banking relationships. The proposal targets both the onboarding of new operators and the operational scope of existing arrangements that touch crypto assets.

Virtual asset service providers operate at the intersection of traditional finance and crypto infrastructure, handling custody, exchange, and transfer functions. Enhanced monitoring and transaction limits would restrict how these providers interact with registered payment operators.

The proposal does not establish a permanent ban but rather a 12-month moratorium on new registrations, suggesting a review period during which the central bank intends to formalize permanent rules. The specifics of transaction limits, monitoring thresholds, and enforcement mechanisms have not been detailed in available reporting.
